description: A single-panel figure that is entirely a rendered table specifying the layer-by-layer architecture of a conditional GAN (CGAN) used for machine-learning design of Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si steel. The table is divided into two halves — "Generator network" (left) and "Discriminator network" (right) — each with the columns "Layer name", "Architecture" and "Detail". Generator: input layer = Random noise, 100; Hidden layer 1 = Dense layer 64; Hidden layer 2 = Dense layer 128; Output layer = "Feature + property", 12(11 + 1); Activation Relu (hidden) and Tanh (output); Batch normalization Yes in both hidden layers; Regularizer L2 = 0.01 in every layer. Discriminator: input layer = "Feature + property", 12(11 + 1); Hidden layer 1 = Dense layer 128; Hidden layer 2 = Dense layer 64; Output layer = Dense layer 1; Activation Relu (hidden) and Sigmoid (output); Batch normalization Yes; Regularizer L2 = 0.01 throughout. The mirror-symmetric hidden-layer widths (64→128 in the generator vs 128→64 in the discriminator) show the two networks are inverted twins. The table therefore defines the generative model that maps a 100-dimensional noise vector onto a 12-dimensional vector of 11 features plus 1 property, and the discriminator that scores such 11-feature + 1-property inputs, but it reports no performance values.

subfigures.description: One table, split into a left 'Generator network' half and a right 'Discriminator network' half, listing layer name, architecture and detail for input layer, hidden layer 1, hidden layer 2 and output layer of each network. Generator: Random noise 100 -> Dense 64 -> Dense 128 -> Feature + property 12(11 + 1), Relu/Tanh, batch normalization Yes, L2 = 0.01. Discriminator: Feature + property 12(11 + 1) -> Dense 128 -> Dense 64 -> Dense 1, Relu/Sigmoid, batch normalization Yes, L2 = 0.01. All cell text is fully legible; no image, curve or micrograph is present.

observations.observation: The figure is a text table only, with no plots, micrographs or images; it tabulates deep-network architectures.
The generator input layer takes 'Random noise' with dimension 100.
The generator contains Dense layer 64 (hidden layer 1) followed by Dense layer 128 (hidden layer 2).
The generator output layer is labelled 'Feature + property' with detail '12(11 + 1)', i.e. 11 features plus 1 property.
The discriminator input layer is labelled 'Feature + property' with detail '12(11 + 1)'.
The discriminator contains Dense layer 128 (hidden layer 1) followed by Dense layer 64 (hidden layer 2), i.e. the reverse of the generator.
The discriminator output layer is Dense layer 1 with Sigmoid activation.
All hidden-layer activations in both networks are Relu; the generator output activation is Tanh.
Batch normalization is set to 'Yes' in hidden layers 1 and 2 of both the generator and the discriminator.
Every regularizer entry in both networks is 'L2 = 0.01'.
No training hyperparameters such as learning rate, epoch count, optimizer or batch size appear in the table.
The caption reproduces the same table content, describing a 'Generator network' and 'Discriminator network' with layer name, architecture and detail columns.
The paper title associates this architecture with extreme high accuracy prediction and design of Fe-C-Cr-Mn-Si steel, but the table itself names no alloy or composition.
